text.p: Paraguay goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert, banned by an Argentine court from playing for 13 months, says he will leave Argentine soccer because he is afraid of being attacked.
"I'm afraid that some madman will shoot me in the back, so I want to leave," he said.
"It hurts a lot of people that a Paraguayan can be as popular as me. They think we should just be on building sites or cleaning houses."
Chilavert, one of the world's best goalkeepers, has been sold by reigning Argentine champions Velez Sarsfield for $3.8 million to agent and businessman Michel Basilevitch.
Basilevitch said Chilavert would continue playing at Velez until the end of the year but it is not clear where he will go after that.
These days, Chilavert makes more headlines for his goalscoring ability and volatile comments than his goalkeeping exploits.
He scored four goals, two penalties and two free-kicks, for his club this year and one for Paraguay when they surprisingly drew with Argentina in Buenos Aires earlier this month.

But just four days later a criminal court in the city of La Plata, some 60 kilometres from Buenos Aires, gave him a three-month suspended prison sentence and banned him from playing football for 13 months.
The penalty was imposed for Chilavert's part in a rumpus on the pitch during a game away to Gimnasia-La Plata.

Chilavert claimed the media knew about the sentence before he and his lawyers did and said it was part of a campaign to stop him playing in the World Cup qualifying matches in which Argentina are struggling.
Chilavert said the ban applied only in Argentine as it was not imposed by soccer authorities. He said he could carry on playing in Argentina itself until an appeal was heard.
Velez have signed former World Cup goalkeeper Sergio Goycochea, currently with Brazilian club Internacional, as the extrovert Paraguayan's replacement.
